is_anopheles.evidence: Tests were performed with susceptible and pyrethroid-resistant strains of Anopheles gambiae to assess the pyrethroid and chlorfenapyr components separately. (Abstract)

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper mentions that resistance in the Covè strain is mediated by the Vgsc L1014F mutation, but it cites a previous study (citation 23: Ngufor et al. 2015) for this characterisation rather than reporting new genotyping data in this study. (Page 4)

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper reports bioassay results (mortality, knockdown, blood-feeding inhibition) and chemical analysis of insecticide content in nets, but does not provide genotype counts, allele counts, or frequencies for any markers.

african_field_population.evidence: An. gambiae s.l. Covè strain is an insecticide-resistant field strain, which is the first filial (F1) progeny of mosquitoes collected from the CREC/LSHTM field station in Covè, southern Benin. (Page 3)

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study evaluating the regeneration time, efficacy, and wash-resistance of a new insecticide-treated net (PermaNet Dual).

sub_country_location.evidence: The mosquitoes were collected from the CREC/LSHTM field station in Covè, southern Benin. (Page 3)

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The paper does not specify the collection years for the field mosquitoes used to establish the F1 progeny.

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study uses the Covè strain, a well-characterised strain from a specific field station in Benin frequently used in PAMVERC evaluations, but the data reported here (net efficacy) is specific to this study.

supplement.evidence: The supporting information files (S1-S5 Tables) are described as containing bioassay results and chemical analysis data, not genotype data.

assessment.summary: This study evaluates the laboratory performance (regeneration time, efficacy, and wash-resistance) of PermaNet Dual, a deltamethrin-chlorfenapyr net, against susceptible (Kisumu) and resistant (Covè) strains of Anopheles gambiae. While the paper identifies the Vgsc L1014F (L995F) mutation as a mechanism of resistance in the Covè strain, it does so by citing previous characterisation work (Ngufor et al. 2015) and does not report any new genotype data.
exclusion_reasons: Does not report extractable genotype data for target markers (mentions L1014F but cites a previous study for the characterisation of the strain used).
